So a quick back story, I'm in the military and live in the barracks and sometimes it can get a bit crowded in our rooms on the weekend drinking and everything. Well, the other day me and some of my buddies were drinking and someone spilled a bit of their white russian onto my case and some of it got through the top vent and got onto some of my hardware. Fortunately the computer was off and I quickly took off the side panel and took a towel and started dabbing away at the wet spots. Surprisingly everything works just fine, no issues. But there are some whiteish spots on the hardware where it dried over. So, I was wondering what the safest way is to clean that off of some of the components inside.
Best way to completely clean hardware?

Usually, a small amount of alcohol (the non-drinking kind) is enough to clean most electronic components. Use little mounts on a q-tip or something similar to soften up the sticky stuff then something that doesn't leave lint behind to wipe it up and off. If you can take it to an area and is reasonably static and dust free it might be easier to take the dirty stuff out so you can get around it better.
I agree with everyone here. I get these in the shop from time to time. We keep about 4 bottles of 90% rubbing alcohol. Works like a charm.

I would recommend 90% or higher Isopropyl alcohol. Normally what they sell at Walgreens or Walmart is antiseptic isopropyl rubbing alcohol that is only 70% alcohol and CAN harm electronics. The 90% or higher will not. If you get the 99% you can actually dip your electronics in it and it won't hurt them at all.

EDIT: Beware - Alcohol CAN harm plastics and screen protectors, as well as possibly some screens depending on the coating. Always test a small area first!
Where can you get 99%? I've only found 90% at my local CVS.
90% will be fine - you have to order 99% online - http://www.amazon.com/Swan-Isopropyl-Alcohol-99-Pint/dp/B00ZOIMORA
I know 90% works, but I think I'm gonna try the 99% because that's what they recommend for the MFLB anyway
Good deal. We usually get it from Staples Plus, but Amazon will get it to you faster unless you have business delivery from Staples.

Used to work in a kitchen. I was a young dude and every other person who worked in the kitchen was pretty young. The kitchen wasn't a super serious one, we didn't have a lot of menu items that required a lot of skill to make, mostly sandwiches and salads, you just had to remember the ingredients and put them on in the correct order, easy. However it was high volume and with the number of people in the kitchen (typically two) you had to work flat out as fast as you could in order to get by without getting behind on tickets. Everyone who worked in the kitchen knew the deal and didn't really have issue with it. It was what it was. Then a new worker I'll call Zee showed up. She was an older woman and easily the slowest worker in the kitchen. Being paired with her was like a death sentence because no matter how hard you worked to pick up her slack you would still fall behind and end up with angry customers and everyone in the restaurant being pissed off.

To top it off, she was hired under some pretext that she was there to help us better adhere to the corporate standards we were supposed to be meeting: things like throwing out onions every morning, even though they had been cut fresh the night before and were kept in a sealed container in a fridge and smelled and tasted perfectly fresh. She started insisting on all these practices that were basically pointless and that radically scaled up the amount of prep we needed to do each day. Before this we were already stretched thin, now with the new practices we basically could never achieve the amount of work we needed to do, while holding the line at the same time, and would always run out of some prep around mid-day no matter how hard we worked, and working with Zee was still a hundred times worse than working with anyone else. Eventually I realized that the best strategy was for me to hold the line and work as fast as I could by myself filling orders while she did the prep at the leisurely pace she usually worked at, because if I did prep, eventually I would have to help her on the line because she couldn't keep up and then we would have two people trying to catch up on line and no prep getting done. Not to mention she was so slow on line and forgetful that she would FUCK SHIT UP and we'd have to make a lot of orders twice or she would make shit that I had already made without bothering to take a glance at what was in the window. So, I busted my ass AS HARD AS I FUCKING COULD on the line and it wasn't pretty but for the most part I managed to keep up and gave her time to get some prep done so we would have food to sell at mid day. I felt pretty good about finally having a good day with Zee until I realised she was actually upset that I had done this. I'm not kidding. She was upset that I hadn't called for help when it got busy on the line and almost broke down in tears when telling me about it. Keep in mind that when working with other people it was standard practice for one to hold the line as long as possible while the other busted out prep as fast as possible. Usually line needed help around lunch time but by this time the person doing prep would have finished most of their shit because they worked fast because they knew it was a race against time. Zee never got close to clearing the prep because she was so fucking slow. I tried to explain my thinking to her but she was taking it personally and couldn't seem to see reason. I'm generally a nice guy and she was so upset that I kinda started to feel bad and apologized to her, despite not really feeling like I had done anything wrong, but the more I thought about it later the more I wanted to punch her in the face. She was TOO FUCKING OLD AND SLOW to work there. Harsh reality but there it is. Her presence in that kitchen was a burden on every other worker and she was obnoxious enough to make us feel bad for making her feel bad about herself, and it wasn't even intentional, nobody told her off or said anything negative, she was just upset by the fact that we had to work harder to pick up her slack but nobody knew what she expected us to do, just let us fail? When we see something that needs done we would do it as fast as possible and she would get upset that we were doing all the stuff that she was about to do. Fuck that stupid idiot bitch.

Outside of work she was a perfectly sweet lady and we got along fine, but at work she made my life hell and I hated her for it.
